title: Indian Student on F-1 Visa Arrested in Germany After Allegedly Killing Girlfriend in Arizona
excerpt: Varun Batchigari, 20, fled Tucson within hours of the alleged strangulation of 19-year-old Julissa Salazar, but a multi-agency FBI operation intercepted him in Munich before he could reach India.
body:
• Varun Batchigari, a 20-year-old Indian national on an F-1 student visa, was arrested in Munich after allegedly strangling his 19-year-old girlfriend Julissa Rubi Salazar in their Tucson apartment.
  • Batchigari allegedly stole Salazar's phone and credit cards after the killing and sent fake text messages to her mother to conceal the crime before fleeing to Germany on a flight bound for India.
  • A felony warrant reveals allegations of prior domestic violence, a sexual assault accusation, and Batchigari's expulsion from the University of Arizona following a fight.
  • The FBI coordinated with five federal agencies and Munich police to intercept Batchigari at the airport. He faces first-degree murder and kidnapping charges and awaits extradition to Arizona.

An Indian national studying in the United States on an F-1 student visa was arrested at a German airport after allegedly killing his 19-year-old girlfriend in a Tucson apartment, then fleeing the country within hours in an attempt to reach India, according to the Tucson Police Department and federal law enforcement sources.

Varun Batchigari, 20, faces charges of first-degree murder and kidnapping in the death of Julissa Rubi Salazar, a University of Arizona student who was found dead with signs of strangulation in her off-campus apartment on the afternoon of August 6.

The Crime and the Flight

Salazar's family requested a welfare check after receiving text messages from her phone that raised their concern. When Tucson Fire Department medics arrived at the apartment complex near Tyndall Avenue and Adams Street — just minutes from the university campus — they found Salazar dead in her bedroom with a blanket pulled up to her neck, according to a felony warrant obtained by KOLD-TV.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2086634805870088391

Investigators determined that Batchigari had allegedly stolen Salazar's cellphone and credit cards after the killing and sent a series of text messages to her mother while posing as the victim, according to the Tucson Police Department. The deceptive messages prompted the family's concern and ultimately led to the discovery of Salazar's body.

By the time detectives identified Batchigari as the suspect, he had already left Tucson. According to Tucson police spokesperson Francisco Magos, Batchigari boarded a flight from Tucson to Houston, then connected to a Berlin-bound flight with plans to continue on to India.

International Arrest

Tucson police coordinated with five federal agencies — the FBI Tucson Office, the FBI Legal Attaché Office in Berlin, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, and the U.S. Marshals Service — along with the Munich Police Department to intercept Batchigari the moment he landed in Germany.

"The Tucson Police Department is grateful for the assistance and coordination provided by our federal and international partners. Their efforts were instrumental in locating Batchigari and coordinating with authorities in Germany."

— Tucson Police Department

Batchigari was taken into custody in Munich and is being held as he awaits extradition back to Arizona, where he will be booked into the Pima County Adult Detention Complex.

A Pattern of Violence

The felony warrant paints a troubling picture of escalating violence in the months before Salazar's death. Witnesses told investigators that Salazar had moved out of a shared living arrangement after experiencing problems with Batchigari in late 2025 and had planned to end the relationship because of an alleged history of domestic violence, according to Fox News.

Salazar's roommates reported hearing loud screaming from her room that lasted several minutes on August 5, the day before her body was discovered, according to KOLD-TV. When they texted to check on her, they received a reply saying she was fine and it had just been an argument.

The warrant also includes a separate allegation from a witness who told investigators that Batchigari sexually assaulted her at a Halloween party, though she said she never reported it to law enforcement. Another witness said Batchigari had been expelled from the University of Arizona following a fight and subsequently lost his job, leading to financial problems.

Visa Status Questions

Federal law enforcement sources told Fox News that Batchigari entered the United States through Los Angeles International Airport on January 8, 2024, on an F-1 student visa. He had been studying business analytics at the University of Arizona before his expulsion.

Federal records reviewed by Fox News show that Batchigari remained in lawful immigration status at the time of the alleged murder despite his reported expulsion. International students on F-1 visas are generally required to maintain enrollment to keep their legal status, raising questions about how his status had not been flagged.

Community Response

A GoFundMe campaign has been set up to support the Salazar family. "There are no words that can make this loss easier, but we hope that by coming together as a community, we can help ease some of the financial burden," organizer Paola Fernandez wrote.

The case is likely to draw scrutiny from both immigration policy advocates and law enforcement officials over visa monitoring protocols and the speed of the international response that prevented Batchigari from reaching India.
image_caption: Julissa Rubi Salazar, 19, was found dead in her apartment near the University of Arizona campus in Tucson. Her boyfriend Varun Batchigari was arrested in Munich after fleeing the country on a flight bound for India.
nri_angle: The case raises questions about F-1 student visa monitoring and oversight gaps when students lose enrollment status.
